# Mixed-state triangle moments and the exact depth of three centered homothets

This note proves an all-state angular classification for exactly three centered homothetic triangle fibers. Its broader result is an exact joint moment/Hessian identity for arbitrary finite base sets. Neither result is a classification for arbitrary translated fibers. The affine-centroid graph class already satisfies OC by the archived weighted-base-center argument; the value here is the exact calibration of moving normals, including genuinely two-vertex traces.

## 1. Coordinates and the general proper-cell identity

Put

    T=conv{(-1,-1),(2,-1),(-1,2)},   |T|=9/2.

Let P be any finite subset of R^n, z0 in P, and let r_z>0. The fibers are r_z T and the source is the ACTUAL point (z0,0). No radius concavity is needed in this section. By a permutation of the three vertices (a linear, area-preserving symmetry of T) and positive rescaling of a nonzero continuous normal, every such normal has the form u=(1,theta), 0<=theta<=1. Indeed its minimum, maximum and remaining vertex values can be assigned to the displayed first, second and third vertices; their sum is zero, and the ratio of the last-minus-first gap to the second-minus-first gap is theta. The integer normal is rescaled by the same positive factor.

Consider the actual ambient cap

    x1+theta*x2+alpha.(z-z0)>=0.

Write t_z=z-z0, k_z=alpha.t_z, and s=1-theta. For 0<theta<1 its fiber volume is

    0                                  if k_z<=-(2-theta)r_z,
    a_z^2/(2s)                         if -(2-theta)r_z<=k_z<=(1-2theta)r_z,
    (9/2)r_z^2-b_z^2/(2theta)          if (1-2theta)r_z<=k_z<=(1+theta)r_z,
    (9/2)r_z^2                         if k_z>=(1+theta)r_z,

where

    a_z=(2-theta)r_z+k_z,   b_z=(1+theta)r_z-k_z,   a_z+b_z=3r_z.       (1)

The two proper states will be called I and J, respectively. I is a one-vertex captured cap; J has a one-vertex residual. These formulas follow by taking the two edge intercepts of the appropriate corner triangle, whose products are a_z^2/[9s r_z^2] and b_z^2/[9theta r_z^2]. They agree in value and first derivative at the middle-vertex transition. At the empty/full transitions the first derivatives also agree, since the disappearing triangle has zero squared height.

Let ell_z be the length of the cut section measured in its x2 coordinate (Euclidean section length is sqrt(1+theta^2) times this):

    ell_z=a_z/s in I,   ell_z=b_z/theta in J,   ell_z=0 in a strict saturated state. (2)

At a support transition use ell_z=0; at a middle-vertex transition either formula gives ell_z=3r_z. The volume sum Q is C^1 in (alpha,theta) for 0<theta<1. Direct differentiation gives, including at every transition,

    grad_alpha Q=sum_z ell_z t_z,
    Q_theta=sum_z (ell_z^2/2-r_z ell_z).                              (3)

Consequently an interior local minimum must satisfy

    sum_z ell_z t_z=0,
    sum_z ell_z^2=2 sum_z r_z ell_z.                                  (4)

For a strict trace cell, put v_z=(t_z,ell_z-r_z) in R^(n+1). The FULL Hessian is

    D^2 Q=(1/s) sum_(z in I) v_z v_z^T
                -(1/theta) sum_(z in J) v_z v_z^T.                    (5)

In fact d ell/dtheta=(ell-r)/s in I and -(ell-r)/theta in J; d ell/dalpha is respectively t/s and -t/theta. Differentiating (3) gives every block of (5). Thus a local minimum in a strict cell must have the signed matrix in (5) positive semidefinite, not merely a nonnegative angular second derivative.

There is also an exact allocation balance. Put

    T_I=sum_I r ell, T_J=sum_J r ell, T=T_I+T_J,
    S_I=sum_I ell^2, S_J=sum_J ell^2.

Taking the dot product of the first equation in (4) with alpha, and using
k=s ell-(2-theta)r in I and k=(1+theta)r-theta ell in J, gives

    S_I=3T_I-sT,   S_J=3T_J-theta T,                                  (6)

or equivalently

    sum_I ell(3r-ell)=sT,   sum_J ell(3r-ell)=theta T.

In addition, if r is concave on conv(P), the positive weights ell_z and the first equation in (4) imply

    T<=r_(z0) sum_z ell_z,
    sum_z ell_z^2<=2r_(z0) sum_z ell_z.                                (7)

Here the total section weight is positive because the source cut is proper. For theta<1/2 every strict J index has alpha.t_z>(1-2theta)r_z>0. These identities are necessary conditions, not a proof that every longer concave chain has canonical critical directions.

## 2. Three-fiber angular exclusion, including transitions

Take P={-1,0,1}, source0, and radii

    r_-1=a>0, r_0=c>0, r_1=b>0.

At this point a,b,c need not satisfy concavity. The volume at the middle centroid has an attained minimum: for a normalized continuous normal in the compact circle, both endpoint traces saturate once |alpha| exceeds a uniform bound. Clamping alpha at that bound preserves both endpoint traces and the source trace. The volume is continuous, so minimization is over a compact parameter set. Purely integer caps through the source contain its entire positive fiber and at least one entire endpoint; a sufficiently large finite integer tilt with a fixed continuous direction retains those strict endpoint statuses and replaces the full source fiber by a proper cap of smaller area. Caps containing the source may first be moved parallel until their boundary passes through it, which only decreases their volume. Thus it suffices to minimize the displayed nonvertical through-source caps.

Suppose a minimizer has 0<theta<1. If alpha=0, every fiber cut passes through its centroid. Its section length is greater than 2r_z, so every summand ell_z^2/2-r_z ell_z in (3) is strictly positive. This contradicts Q_theta=0. Reflecting the integer coordinate and interchanging a,b if needed, assume alpha>0.

The integer first-order condition gives

    ell_-=ell_+=l.

If l=0, both endpoint contributions to Q_theta vanish, while the source contribution is positive, again a contradiction. Hence l>0: no endpoint can be full, empty, or at a support transition. The source section length is

    L=(2-theta)c/s       for theta<=1/2,
    L=(1+theta)c/theta   for theta>=1/2.                               (8)

For 0<theta<1, L>2c. Angular stationarity therefore gives

    l(a+b-l)=L(L-2c)/2>0.                                             (9)

In particular D:=a+b>l.

If both endpoints are in I, their equal section lengths give
2s l=(2-theta)D, hence l>D, impossible. If both are in J, they give
2theta l=(1+theta)D, also l>D. A left J/right I pair is impossible: a left J requires theta>1/2 since its k=-alpha<0, whereas a right I requires theta<1/2 since its k=alpha>0. Thus only a left I/right J pair remains, allowing for the moment a middle-vertex transition.

The two width equations are

    alpha=(2-theta)a-s l=(1+theta)b-theta l,
    3a=(1+theta)D+(1-2theta)l,
    3b=(2-theta)D-(1-2theta)l.                                        (10)

A left middle-vertex transition l=3a would force
D=2theta l/(1+theta)<l. A right such transition l=3b would force
D=2s l/(2-theta)<l. Both contradict (9). Therefore the endpoint states I,J are strict.

If theta<1/2, the source is I and contributes no alpha-alpha derivative. Formula (5) gives

    Q_(alpha alpha)=1/s-1/theta<0,

excluding a local minimum.

If theta>1/2, the source is J. The determinant of the endpoint Hessian is

    -(D-2l)^2/(s theta).

The source adds only the theta-theta entry -(L-c)^2/theta, while
Q_(alpha alpha)=1/s-1/theta>0. Hence the full determinant is

    -(D-2l)^2/(s theta)
       -((L-c)^2/theta)(1/s-1/theta)<0.                              (11)

The Hessian is not positive semidefinite, excluding a local minimum.

It remains to treat theta=1/2, where the source itself is at its middle-vertex transition. The first derivatives still vanish. Use the one-sided cell theta>1/2, in which the source is J and the endpoints remain strictly I,J for sufficiently small perturbations. At theta=1/2, (10) forces a=b. The one-sided Hessian has

    H_(alpha alpha)=0,
    H_(alpha theta)=2(a+b-2l).

If this off-diagonal entry is nonzero, take a direction with delta theta>0 and choose the sign and finite magnitude of delta alpha so that its quadratic form is negative. The resulting ray stays in the stated cell for a sufficiently small step. If the off-diagonal entry is zero, then a=b=l. The endpoint theta-theta entries cancel, and the source contributes -8c^2. Taking delta alpha=0, delta theta>0 gives a negative second variation. The one-sided Taylor expansion is valid because the source formula is a smooth rational function up to this transition from that side. This excludes the last case.

We have proved: for arbitrary positive a,b,c, every minimum at the middle centroid has a canonical or opposite-canonical continuous normal. No endpoint saturation, endpoint vertex transition, or source vertex transition was omitted.

## 3. The exact one-dimensional tilt extrema

For r>0 put

    f_r(k)=0                              for k<=-2r,
           (2r+k)^2/2                     for -2r<=k<=r,
           (9/2)r^2                       for k>=r.                   (12)

The canonical cap volume at the middle centroid is

    Q_+(alpha)=2c^2+f_a(-alpha)+f_b(alpha).

Let g(alpha)=f_a(-alpha)+f_b(alpha). Its exact extrema are

    min g=min{(a+b)^2,(9/2)a^2,(9/2)b^2},                             (13)

    max g=max{(9/2)a^2+(2b-a)_+^2/2,
              (9/2)b^2+(2a-b)_+^2/2}.                               (14)

Here x_+=max(x,0). To verify completeness, on every interval cut out by
alpha=-a,2a,-2b,b, either both terms are proper quadratics, one term is a monotone proper quadratic and the other constant, or both are constant. A strict internal minimum can therefore occur only in the both-proper interval, where g is a strictly convex quadratic with stationary point alpha=a-b and value (a+b)^2, or on a saturation plateau with value (9/2)a^2 or (9/2)b^2. The stationary point is feasible exactly when a/2<=b<=2a. If b>2a, then (a+b)^2>9a^2>(9/2)a^2; the symmetric argument applies if a>2b. Thus retaining the possibly infeasible square candidate in (13) does not change the answer. At either full transition alpha=-a or alpha=b, the derivative jumps downward, so no additional strict minimum occurs there. Empty transitions have continuous derivative and supply no new minimum except an already listed plateau.

For a maximum, the both-proper quadratic has its maximum on interval endpoints, and each one-proper interval is monotone. Only full transitions alpha=-a,b or plateaus need be tested. Their values are the two expressions in (14); each includes its corresponding plateau value. This proves (14), also when breakpoints coincide.

Opposite-canonical caps are complements, up to a null line section, of canonical caps with reversed tilt. Thus their minimum is

    Q_-min=(5/2)c^2+(9/2)(a^2+b^2)-max g.                            (15)

Equations (13)--(15), together with Section 2, are an exact finite formula for arbitrary three positive centered fibers, even without actual convex compatibility.

## 4. Actual midpoint compatibility removes the opposite directions

The three centered homothets are compatible with an actual convex body exactly when

    c>=(a+b)/2.                                                       (16)

Necessity follows from (aT+bT)/2=((a+b)/2)T subset cT. Sufficiency follows by taking the hypograph of the positive piecewise-affine concave radius on [-1,1]:

    C={(z,x):-1<=z<=1, x in r(z)T},

which is a full-dimensional compact convex body and has exactly the specified three integer fibers.

Assume (16), and interchange the endpoints so that a<=b. The second expression in (14) is the larger one. When b<=2a the difference second-minus-first is 3(b^2-a^2). When b>=2a the difference is (5/2)b^2+2ab-5a^2>0. Hence

    Q_-min=(5/2)c^2+(9/2)a^2-(2a-b)_+^2/2,
    Q_+min=2c^2+min{(a+b)^2,(9/2)a^2}.                               (17)

If b>=2a, their difference is c^2/2>0. If a<=b<2a, using (16) and bounding the minimum in (17) separately by each candidate gives the two valid lower bounds

    Q_-min-Q_+min >= (a+b)(13a-11b)/8,
    Q_-min-Q_+min >= 3(b-a)(5a-b)/8.                                 (18)

For a<=b<13a/11 the first is positive. For 13a/11<=b<2a the second is positive. Thus Q_-min>Q_+min always.

Consequently the EXACT raw depth of the middle centroid of the actual body is

    D0=2c^2+min{(a+b)^2,(9/2)a^2,(9/2)b^2},                         (19)

and every minimizing continuous normal is one of the three canonical vertex directions. Formula (19) includes the switch from a both-proper optimized cap to a full/empty endpoint cap.

## 5. All centers and the exact global maximum

For completeness, every fiber centroid maximizes mixed depth within its own fiber. Indeed the mixed measure and its support are invariant under the finite linear symmetry group permuting the triangle vertices. Each depth superlevel set is convex: if a halfspace contains a convex combination of two points, it contains at least one endpoint, so the depth at that combination is at least the smaller endpoint depth. Averaging a point over the permutation group gives its fiber centroid. Thus the centroid has at least the original point's depth.

At an endpoint fiber, the centroid depth is exactly 2a^2 or 2b^2. Every cap containing that centroid captures at least its ordinary triangle centroid bound 2r^2 in the source fiber. Conversely choose an ordinary canonical centroid cap and a sufficiently large integer tilt to exclude both other fibers completely. For an arbitrary point in that endpoint fiber, the same finite isolation permits its ordinary depth, which is at most the centroid depth. At the middle fiber, the preceding symmetry argument and (19) apply. Hence the EXACT global raw maximum is

    max{2a^2, 2b^2, 2c^2+min{(a+b)^2,(9/2)a^2,(9/2)b^2}}.            (20)

The total mixed area is (9/2)(a^2+c^2+b^2); normalized depth is (20) divided by this number. All centers discussed belong to the original fibers, and all oblique normals were included before minimization. There are no masses on nonvertical boundaries because the fibers are positive planar bodies; purely integer boundary mass was handled directly in Section 2.

As a consistency check, (20) implies the planar n=1 OC constant 2/9 for this already-covered affine-centroid class. Scale c=1 and write a<=b. If b^2>=1+a^2, the endpoint value 2b^2 is at least 1+a^2+b^2. Otherwise both (a+b)^2 and (9/2)a^2 exceed a^2+b^2-1: the first does so by 2ab+1, and the second by 1+(7/2)a^2-b^2>(5/2)a^2. Then the middle value in (20) exceeds 1+a^2+b^2, which is 2/9 of the total mass. This consistency check is not presented as a new OC regime.
